title: WarHub Paint Catalog
description: A consolidated or per-brand paint catalog document. Cross-brand Delta-E equivalents are embedded per paint.

id.description: brand-slug/paint-slug, fully slugged and all-lowercase. Qualified by set (then product code, then hex) when a name collides, so an id depends only on the paint it names. NOTE this is STRICTER than product-catalog.json's id pattern, which preserves manufacturer casing -- the two grammars differ on purpose; see that schema.

role.description: WHAT THIS PRODUCT IS FOR. `category` is the constant `paint` for everything a maker's chart lists -- a liquid, paste, powder or aerosol sold inside a painting range, colour or not -- so this is the key that tells a varnish, thinner, primer, texture paste or pigment jar from a colour. `colour` deposits colour (its finer grain -- wash, contrast, metallic, spray -- stays in `type`/`finish` and is never repeated here); `primer` is undercoat, coloured or clear; `varnish` a clear coat of any sheen; `medium` goes into or under the paint (mixing/glaze mediums, thinners, retarders, flow improvers, flattening bases, masking fluids, decal solutions); `cleaner` does not go into the paint (airbrush/brush cleaners, restorers, strippers); `texture` is a paste, gel or ground with body; `pigment` a dry powder. `applicator`, `tool`, `basing` and `build` name hobby hardware a chart should never list but a harvest can. Present on every paint the archive publishes, and a `varnish`, `medium` or `cleaner` always carries `colourless: true` beside it -- the paint tool refuses to write an archive where either fails to hold.

weightG.description: NET CONTENTS in grams, for a paint sold by mass rather than by volume (a foam-primer tub, a dry pigment weighed rather than jarred). A sibling of volumeMl, not a replacement: either, both or neither may be present, and a consumer that reads only volumeMl behaves exactly as it did before this key existed. NOT a shipping weight.

productIds.description: Product records sharing a barcode with this paint -- the retail SKUs this colour ships as. Plural: one colour is many SKUs. Omitted when there is none. See barcode-index.json.

soldSeparately.description: `false` when a source states this paint is obtainable ONLY inside a boxed set, never as a pot of its own. ABSENT whenever no source said -- which is nearly always, and is a different claim from `true`. Nothing writes `true` today: no source states the positive, so asserting it on every listed paint would publish a fact nobody made; the value stays reserved for a source that one day says it in words. Deliberately a SIBLING of availability rather than another value inside it -- availability and status are free strings consumers filter on, and a new value there would silently drop exactly the set-exclusive records this key exists to keep reachable. A consumer that ignores this key behaves as it did before the key existed.

colourless.description: `true` when the product HAS no colour -- a mixing medium, thinner, varnish, sealer, flow improver, retarder or cleaner. It exists because an absent `hex` already means something else: for 323 of the 391 hexless records it means the colour has not been harvested yet, and the next chart pass fills exactly those. Without this key a consumer cannot distinguish the two, and the catalog itself could not either -- 94 of these products used to carry a stand-in (48 of them exactly #FFFFFF), which put clear varnishes into the colour-equivalence graph as real colours. ABSENT whenever nobody stated it; nothing writes `false`.
